newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: RABOBANK SEES SUBSTANTIAL GROWTH IN '97.
newsitem.headline: RABOBANK SEES SUBSTANTIAL GROWTH IN '97.

text.p: Dutch cooperative bank Rabobank Nederland BA said on Thursday it expected business volumes to show double-digit growth in 1997.
"In line with this trend we also expect a substantial profit rise," chairman Herman Wijffels was quoted as saying in a press release.
Previously, the bank said it expected considerable growth in 1996 net earnings and a major increase in volume terms.
Rabo posted 1996 net profits of 1.63 billion guilders, up 14 percent from 1.43 billion in the previous year.
Rabo said demand for products and services had shown hefty growth in the first quarter. Wijffels called this a "burgeoning trend" in the annual meeting of Rabo's local member banks representatives.
Rabo did not give first quarter profit figures but said total outstanding credit had grown by 13.9 billion guilders to 233.7 billion.

Two-thirds of this increase was taken up by individuals and the remaining part by business clients. Higher demand for credits by private customers was almost entirely caused by continuing demand for mortgages, the bank said.
Clients' deposits totalled 191.8 billion guilders in the first quarter of 1997, up 15.9 billion from the year-ago period.

Part of this rise was caused by last year's takeover of 50 percent of the management vehicle of the Robeco group of investment funds. Rabo has an option to buy the other half of the management group at a later date.
Rabo said fee income at its merchant bank division had shown considerable first-quarter growth but did not give details.
